[2026-09-24 23:26] nikebones : So if I've context clue'd correctly, it sounds like there is a penalty of some sort for redshirting 3 star+ players, and I'm guessing the penalty diminishes as the player gets older? And it's position specific, so if I redshirt Ty Hook I don't get a penalty when recruiting a big?
[2026-09-24 23:28] nikebones : In my head I think of it like this; if I'm a 5 star guard why would I choose to go somewhere that just recruited and redshirted a 5 star guard the season before.
[2026-09-24 23:32] gards710 : Kinda. Theres a penalty for redshirting any player, but the penalty is smaller the less stars the player is, so usually the hit from redshirting a 1 or 2 star player is offset by them getting older/other players graduating/the flip.  Yes, the penalty diminishes as the player gets older/as time passes. But presumably you are redshirting other players as well.  The largest impact is probably position-specific, but it’s not entirely. Redshirting a 5* will still affect recruiting for any player. It likely just hits the hardest on a player at that position, although positions are kinda nebulous early in college and in hs
[2026-09-24 23:57] nikebones : Gotcha gotcha that makes sense, thanks for all that clarification.

[2020-03-03 21:51] thewalkon69 : Im new to OCB, and i took over a Vermont team that is getting demoted. Do yall have any advice on tactics, how to build a squad etc?
[2020-03-03 22:48] dcm2022 : tactics, I'd take a good look at the makeup of who will be your starters for the offensive focus, and try to keep it balanced (there's a percentage for zone, a percentage for pressure, the rest is used for man to man, but that's a hidden stat)
[2020-03-03 22:52] dcm2022 : as for building a squad, the most important singular trait is size. This is a big man's game, and how well you perform inside and on defense is mostly focused on how good your big men are. outside of that, the best way to build a squad is to recruit (you can recruit earlier than seniors in this game, but they can't commit until they are seniors), try to figure out your biggest holes on the team (passing/handling from the PGs, JS/JR from the SGs, etc) and fill as needed.  Don't worry about recruiting players with 12 POT or big men with 11 POT, the dev track is more important (Minutes played seems to be a factor in how much they grow), and you have them for 5 seasons tops, so there's a chance they won't cap until like their senior/RS SR years of college, if that.
[2020-03-04 00:58] furysk : In your shoes, and in no particular order....

Maybe target your 3 favorite guys that currently have 0 or 1 team looking at them at no more than low interest, that are within your region.  You may have to spend the most to recruit a big first.

[2020-03-18 23:24] tps2.0. : I think the target goal for prospects differ on a few things. Right now I can think of four factors that plays into how many contacts I give someone. Note: These are general rules because each player is obviously different.  1. Skill/Star ranking of prospect. I tend to put more contacts into the higher rated players because teams usually go after these guys pretty seriously.  2. Location. Since you get a boost for the players in your region, you don’t have to put in to many contacts to jump up interest levels with a player. I also don’t have to open as much of an “interest lead” on an in region player because I can easily put more contacts on these players to open back up a lead on a guy if I lost it.  3. Time of commitment A player who is willing to commit early means I just need to be leading the sprint. That means I don’t really have to put to many contacts in on the guy to see where he commits. The guys who wait to commit usually means for me that I have to open up a bigger lead, so it is harder for teams who have lost their initial prospects to catch up to me. 4. Level of competition If a bunch of ownerless division three teams have interest in my player, I tend to spend my contacts somewhere else. The opposite is true for teams with owners especially if there division 1. Also make sure to check later on in the year if a few of your competitors ends up running out of scholarships. If they are full, you don’t have to worry about the team stealing the recruit from you. Also, when you recruit HS FR-JR and JUCO FR take now how they finish the year. A promotion can raise the prospects interest after the season, and a demotion can lower a prospect’s interest. Through a relatively small sample size, it seems that promotion causes a positive effect more than demotion causes a negative effect.

[2020-03-26 00:17] furysk : i can quote what steve said about it
[2020-03-26 00:17] furysk : "Each team is capable of making one Half-Time adjustment. Which HT adjustment depends on the score at the half. Use the lower and upper thresholds to trigger the adjustments. If you are way ahead at HT, maybe you want to slow down the pace -- lower threshold >= +15, upper threshold none. Ergo if you're up by 15 or more points, then you trigger that adjustment."
[2020-03-26 00:18] furysk : lower threshold is the minimum requirement, upper is the maximum.

[2020-05-19 22:57] furysk : at the end of the day, the big thing that you will learn is you have to get ahead as far as recruiting goes.
[2020-05-19 22:57] furysk : you have a team right now that is decent because the person before you did enough recruiting to give you respectable SI's across players.
[2020-05-19 23:01] furysk : however, at the end of the day, you'll find that seniors that have very good skillsets are at high interest, and it'll be impossible to kinda work towards them.
[2020-05-19 23:01] furysk : so as hodge noted, pick the best of the rest regionally
[2020-05-19 23:02] furysk : and try to recruit only 3 or 4 guys at maximum in any one season
[2020-05-19 23:03] furysk : your end goal is to 'push recruiting out'.
[2020-05-19 23:03] furysk : which means ideally you get your recruiting mostly done by the 40th week of this season, and you can spend all remaining points on HS-JR
[2020-05-19 23:03] furysk : and then the following year commit more points to juniors quicker and maybe some sophomores.
[2020-05-19 23:04] furysk : until eventually you have most of your coverage on immediate talent two years out and only have to add points due to competition as needed while you recruit several classes out.
[2020-05-19 23:05] furysk : for D.VI, you need a starting 7 of about a 135 average to be competitive for promotion,.

[2020-09-21 01:07] naph7777 : I come from a drivethelane.com background where recruiting is handled very differently. You get X recruiting points per week. All the players sign at season rollover... so you set some priorities on who you want the most on your recruiting board... then hope for the best on signing day.
[2020-09-21 01:07] naph7777 : So the secret to that game is working out how to get decent leads (guys you are guaranteed the opportunity to sign)... then getting lucky enough of the lotteries on the best players.

My mistake on **driving** (which is how you break down and penetrate), where **finishing** (finish going to the basketball off a fast break or a rebound) would be more relevant in this offense

I would probably redshirt Daniel, Landers and (maybe) Fernandes if you want to give him some extra time to be a rotation player by his 5th year. If not on Fernandes I get it. But for Daniel and Landers, you have other good options at those spots (Wyatt, Lawton and Miller at the 2, specifically) to give those guys the year to develop behind the scenes. I think even with redshirting those freshmen you have a good chance to promote if you play your cards right. Maybe try to get a little more shooting in your next recruiting class though, just to help balance it out because some of your underclassmen currently might struggle there in the future.

[2021-04-07 01:07] furysk : with regards to the MIN/ODU strategy, what i used to do in buzzerbeater when playing there, especially on the u21 side where the differences were very small, is i went at it attacking their weakest player when i was on defense rather than trying to stop their strongest.
[2021-04-07 01:08] furysk : so with teams that had a mediocre PG/SG/SF, i would try to make it to where it was much harder to get a clean shot inside, either by running a 3-2 zone if their passing was too low to effectively get it inside that often (or if the game rarely gave their PG more than 3-4 assists, and their team total was poor).
[2021-04-07 01:11] furysk : or by going after their bigs in a more conventional man matchup since most of my bigs were quite defensive in nature (equal to about 14's and 15's here).  I feel like you didn't have the ID to do a more conventional man structure, and while his guards were good at passing i probably would've buffed up a zone/pressure scheme with 35-40% pressure minimum and closer to 25-30% zone to try to make the PG or SG shoot when he didn't want them to at all.

[2021-05-22 22:44] g10rsh : I think to some extent si growth speed is a factor of how grouped/spread out the remaining skill points are. [2021-06-13 22:26] naph7777 : Man to man should have more like for like matchups (PG guarding PG, PF vs PF etc). So if you have a foul-prone, poor-defender that’s in for their offence, and you can put them at the same position as a non-scoring threat, then I think you can hide them with Man better.
[2021-06-13 22:27] tps2.0. : I guess technically in real life it would be height instead of strength.
[2021-06-13 22:28] naph7777 : I also factor in individual strengths. If I have guys with really lop-sides defensive abilities, I’m more likely to lean towards Zone. I want my high ID, low PD guys in the paint all the time. Same for low ID, high PD guards.
[2021-06-13 22:30] naph7777 : In real life it’s kind of the opposite. It’s really easy to put your gun shooter on the wing with their worst PD guy. You set your post up on the block of their worst ID guy. But I don’t think the game engine does that.
[2021-06-13 22:32] tps2.0. : I'm almost positive it doesn't do that. I've manually switched my SG and SF before even though my SG has been almost a foot smaller than some of the really big perimeter players.
[2021-06-13 22:35] naph7777 : I suspect the logic is more like. 1) determine shot location 2) determine primary defender - zone/man setting effects probability 3) add some “team defense” factor based on other players on the court and coach defense. 4) compare relevant shooting, passing and other factors for the offence against all the defense factors. RNG to determine outcome.
[2021-06-13 22:38] naph7777 : Then man/zone will also provide certain bonuses and penalties for other checks. It’s generally agreed that it’s harder for the defense to rebound in a zone for example. But exactly what those bonuses and penalties are is hard to determine.
[2021-06-13 22:42] naph7777 : I really wish the manual was more explicit on what the bonuses and penalties were. It would be nice to know what the trade-offs are.
[2021-06-13 22:49] slickandjakenillinois : I like having to try and figure it out.  In my limited experience, I play more zone if the opponent’s IQ is low. I would also think an opponent with good driving guards could destroy a zone too, so I look for that as well.  And if I don’t have defenders who can match up well against the other team, I tend to play more zone and pack the paint and hope the opponent has a cold outside shooting day. I seem to have had decent success playing above my TPI level this way. But I also have a coach with high offense and defense ratings which may also make my team perform better than the ratings show.

[2021-09-08 19:14] gards710 : ok, at the risk of giving too much away, my thoughts, both on playing zone and beating zone: much has already been said. I think first, you need to have the personnel. What does this mean exactly? Is it just the ratings? Is length important? Is it dependent on the coach's ratings? Is there something hidden? I think ALL are true tbh. As El jefe said, some teams just play zone better, others play man better. Not entirely sure why. Is it dependent on the coach? dependent on the players? Ratings - what ratings are important? I'd say mostly OS/RNG, IQ, passing to beat it and PD/ID, IQ, speed to play it successfully. Size, length, and strength will play a factor as well on both aspects.  And El jefe just said it as I am typing this: What is a zone used for in real life? how do you beat a zone in real life? And how can these be applied in Hardwood? What is zone used for in real life? To mess with the opponent and confuse them, to stop a single big threat, especially inside (more defenders paying attention to that player). So how to beat that? You beat a zone in a number of ways - shoot over it (more 3s), beat them on the boards (hard to control this, but have the personnel for it), beat them down the court before they can set up (play fast tempo), have a player in the middle who can pick the defense apart with mid range shooting and passing (can't customize your offense like this in hw).

[2021-09-22 23:21] naph7777 : I'm curious on people's thoughts on scheduling strategy.  When I started I usually scheduled up. But inherited a decent team that became competitive quickly. My reasoning was that I both wanted to give myself an opportunity to boost my RPI and that I would more quickly find out my teams strengths/weaknesses so I'd have a battle tested lineup come conference play.  A while later I noticed that Chowan were scheduling down and sitting older players that were at or nearing their SI cap for the entirety of non-con. As I was starting to encounter that situation and was struggling to get minutes into my young players this seemed pretty sound (even if I didn't like the negative impact on players career numbers). Minor benefit. It also guaranteed keeping some key players healthy.  I pursued that strategy the last 2 seasons, and this year I think it bit me. My cupcake schedule didn't make me question my initial game settings. As a result I didn't really find my best team settings until part of the way through conference play, by which time I'd dug too big of a hole to overcome.  Next year I plan on scheduling up as all of my starting 5 still have (or at least I hope they do!) plenty of development left in them.  Anyway, I'm curious what other people's strategies and reasons are for using different schedule settings.

[2021-10-21 16:53] giambro4277 : I am having trouble building an 8 man rotation. Any advice? I don’t know how should I use the substitution mode and what positions should be the populated ones.
[2021-10-21 16:56] gards710 : usually I use pattern C when using an 8 man rotation. I think B would be ok too
[2021-10-21 16:58] gards710 : but it depends on how your players are covering the 5 positions. combo G (PG/SG), perimeter wing (SG/SF), combo F (SF/PF), combo big (PF/C)
[2021-10-21 17:40] slickandjakenillinois : Agree with Gards, it really depends on how your backups are playing.  The Game Manual under Help on the Website has the different sub patters, these are in the game strategy section.    Here is my example. I have a big off the bench I want to get every minute I can, so he backs up PF and C. I want to choose a substitution pattern that will typically not have the starting PF and C on the bench at the same time.  Mass substitution is out, Substitution A and B have about a 1 minute overlap at the 11-12 minute mark where these starters are likely both on the bench, so I select C since one or the other starter should be on the floor at all times, unless one has foul trouble.
[2021-10-21 17:41] slickandjakenillinois : This allows my backup big to get almost all the minutes backing up PF and C

[2021-10-22 12:49] david118242 : I heard some discussion about recruiting spreadsheets on the TPI podcast. Does anyone have any tips or tricks or thoughts about things they include that are outside the box? I'm thinking about putting something together and I'm curious what other people do
[2021-10-22 13:09] rlawrenceune : size (and speed)>determines position>determines build .... you can have high tpi guys with bad build for their position and vica versa
[2021-10-22 13:10] rlawrenceune : so look at starting freshman size .. project +7.5 inches and +60 pounds (not exact numbers but the median)
[2021-10-22 18:02] slickandjakenillinois : I try to learn how many contacts it takes to move each sub level, meaning moving from Low to Low+ and so on.  I try to determine these numbers on in-state players, in-region players, and out of region players since it takes more the further the player is from in state.  I also try to project where the attributes will be as the player ages.  Then I can compare between players, and also determine which players I may give up on or defend if there is competition, or determine if I want to go after a player who already has interest from another team.
[2021-10-22 18:15] _plokmijn : I recruit on impulse. Probably should find some way to organize my recruiting but I never get around to it
[2021-10-22 18:16] _plokmijn : Main advice is to go for balance across the roster instead of always going for the best recruits. Sometimes a lower ranked big is more impactful than a great guard that’s stuck on the bench
[2021-10-22 18:40] gards710 : I basically do the first half of what <@!704897988572610571> does. I don't so much do the second part haha, but I think he's doing the smart thing with that. It's very general, but the +7.5" is about the median (I believe on the pod where we did this, I said +6" and that was conservative) and the +60 lbs I'd say is actually conservative.

[2021-10-27 15:14] naph7777 : It will start vague. "He seems to understand defense" etc, and a few seasons later it will firm up. If you look through some older coaches you'll see all the different reputations and be able to approximate the range of values for different comments.

[2021-11-05 13:55] david118242 : I want to start doing more opposition planning. Any advice on what to look for? I'm thinking trying to sort out expected lineup, who are the scorers, where are they shooting from, what kind of tempo the opposition plays with and how to counter it, and what defenses they've used. Any other tips?
[2021-11-05 15:10] gards710 : If that's just a "start", I'd hate to know what the finish looks like...that's just about the whole kit and caboodle for me
[2021-11-05 15:11] gards710 : haha, in all seriousness, I'd add where to position your own players offensively, and their green lights (in Game Management), although that can be a seasonal big picture thing than a game to game thing (some people adjust these game to game, some don't)
[2021-11-05 15:18] naph7777 : When I have the time, these are the questions I ask myself when scouting an opponent.  Can I press this team? (Do they have sufficient handling/passing/IQ... also more likely to press if I have a speed advantage).  Does my opponent press? (If yes, I might play a little faster, might up the minutes of better handlers/passers. If not, maybe I can get more minutes into a better scorer/defender who doesn't have so much handling/passing.)  Does my opponent shoot (and make) many 3's? (I may need to extend my defense)  Does my opponent take almost all their shots in close? (I may need to collapse my defense)  Does my opponent have stamina/depth problems? (I might increase the tempo I might also put a scorer/athlete opposite my opponent's key player(s) in the hope of saddling them with foul trouble.)  Does my opponent have a player that draws a lot of fouls? (Is one of my key players going to have to play against him? Can I switch his position? Or do I maybe just play more Zone this game?)  Where positions are my opponents top FGA/Scorers playing? Do they match up with my best defenders? (If yes, I might play more Man so those matchups happen more often. If no I might Zone some more)  Do I think I will win (go faster) or lose (go slower) the possession battle (turnovers/rebounds)?  Is my opponent significantly stronger/weaker in either PDef or IDef? Is it enough of a factor for me to move my usual offensive focus in or out for this opponent?
[2021-11-05 15:19] naph7777 : All of which assumes you actually have enough versatility that those questions matter. Often you work out your best lineup and find that just playing to your own strengths works out better than trying to change everything to counter your opponent.
[2021-11-05 15:23] gards710 : also, consider your half time adjustments. In what scenarios are they triggering? what are the goals of the adjustments? for example, I wouldn't have an adjustment that says "if my opponent hits 10 3s in the first half, I sink my defense -2"
[2021-11-05 16:06] naph7777 : I am really not good at half time adjustments. All ears on that front.
[2021-11-05 16:07] rlawrenceune : -5, 100% zone if leading, +5, 100% man if losing

[2021-11-16 22:42] fuzzy812 : admin Joined: 01/24/2017 Posts: 2066  Administrator It's more about the skills required than the actual distance.  Finishing – shooting skill going to the basketball (fast break, driving or break away steals etc.). It's short distance and may result in a dunk or lay-up or something like that.  Inside Shooting - is from reasonably close and may result in a dunk. But it’s a difference scenario – a offensive player posting up the defender. This skill is the footwork, body control and shooting skills required to counter a defender close to the basket and get a shot off. It will be affected by other skills and attributes like height, strength etc.  Outside Shooting – is a player’s jump shooting ability from anywhere on the court –including the foul line. But there are other factors that may affect this – like Range for longer shots / beyond the arc. A different set of skills and attributes affect these shots as well – speed, distance etc.  Tip-ins are rather unique. It’s not specifically a shooting skill. But there is also a rebound and put back (which would be a rebound followed quickly by a inside shot – but not as single action like a tip-in).  Steve
[2021-11-17 02:07] awoodard_20 : So taking this into game management, would yall equate "i" to more of midrange shooting if you set your perimeter players to that positioning?
[2021-11-17 02:10] fuzzy812 : Steve said something recently about this, "i" for perimeter players relates to more driving
[2021-11-17 02:50] naph7777 : I guess it works something like this: There are a certain number of offensive actions. For the sake of argument lets say there are 4. Post, Drive, Mid-range, Three. (P/D/M/3)  For each position there is a baseline percentage chance of attempting each action. Again this is all guesswork but lets imagine the chances at each position are something like PG: 15/20/30/35 SG: 20/20/30/30 SF: 25/25/25/25 PF: 30/30/20/20 C : 35/30/20/15  I suspect they are probably a little more extreme than that (C's hardly ever shoot 3's unless you put them on "o" or "O"), but you get the idea.  Then each offensive focus provides a modifier to those chances "O" -15/-10/+10/+15 "o" -10/-10/+15/ +5 " " no modifier "i" +5 /+15/-10/-10 "I" +15/+10/-10/-15 (maybe its more or less extreme than this, I don't know) Then you combine the positional baseline chance with the offensive focus modifier to work out the chance of attempting each action for a given player.  C + "I" = 50/40/10/0 SG + "o" = 10/10/40/35 etc.

[2022-01-14 19:54] euphael : for example you have 3 Centers on depth chart....is it possible to set it 31 min, 26 min and 10 min?
[2022-01-14 19:55] gards710 : in the Game Management tab, there is a column for playing time.
[2022-01-14 19:56] gards710 : You can do that, but you shouldn't. The main one that matters is the starter. that will influence how much the backups play
[2022-01-14 19:57] gards710 : so if the starter plays 31 minutes, then only 9 minutes are available for a backup to play. in order for the backup to get 26 minutes, he'd have to play at other positions. Setting that guy to 26 minutes would mean he likely gets ~9 mins at C and 17 mins elsewhere. That's fine to do
[2022-01-14 19:58] gards710 : but that guy for 10 min likely gets nothing except in emergency situations (like foul trouble or injury)
[2022-01-14 19:58] euphael : thats what I want
[2022-01-14 19:58] gards710 : but pretty much never set a guy to 10 (or less than 20). because in the event of an emergency situation, that player at 10 mins would play a MAXIMUM of 10 mins
[2022-01-14 19:59] euphael : so if i set 30 min, 20 min and 20 mins it doesnt mean that 2nd and 3rd will play same amount of mins
[2022-01-14 19:59] slickandjakenillinois : And by emergency, that means foul trouble.  So I set my backups to the max minutes I would want them to play to avoid fatigue anyway.

[2022-01-30 16:03] action_jackson_123_fire : What goes into players being good in an up-tempo offense and a slow paced one? Speed doesn't seem to be a major contributor.
[2022-01-30 16:08] furysk : I'm not of the opinion that anything makes or breaks a build as far as being able to play up tempo.
[2022-01-30 16:09] furysk : With that being said, i do have a preference towards players with a bit more stamina, as my assumption has been that the game engine probably punishes the tempo/pace of play in terms of the fatigue you accumulate on each player during the course of a game.  so going in with 4-5 stamina players on an up tempo offense probably will lead to more injuries or times where you see heavy fatigue on players during the game.
[2022-01-30 16:11] furysk : furthermore, i would argue that Finishing, Driving, and Handling take more precedence in this offensive style than a slower tempo, because all impact the ability to move to the basket with the ball in specific ways.
[2022-01-30 16:11] action_jackson_123_fire : Makes sense thanks! How much do you trust scouting reports? Notes about tempo and such.
[2022-01-30 16:11] furysk : Driving (Drv): ability to break down a defense and penetrate to the basket in order to either pass or shoot.
[2022-01-30 16:11] furysk : Handle (Hnd): ability to handle and move with the basketball.
[2022-01-30 16:12] furysk : Finishing (Fin): ability to finish going to the basketball on a drive or on a fast break.
[2022-01-30 16:15] furysk : On the scouting on tempo, i'm only moderately interested in that.  I figure it's trying to point out that there is a build path that makes the player more or less capable, but unlike steves other game where comments are pretty much king as far as where a player can cap this game the player can often grow beyond the constraints of a comment rating.
[2022-01-30 16:17] furysk : Very few make it out of 8-9 Outside Shot if they have "shoot touch" negative comment, but we've seen a few examples of bad speed getting to 8-9 on players which could be considered more or less ok speed on a PF and just fine on a center.  So if a player has a "struggle in up tempo" but has a build that is pathing into all of the stats i considered above going double digits, i'm less likely to really worry much about the comment.
[2022-01-30 16:18] furysk : however, some believe it has a greater impact, so that's less likely to be more widely agreed with than my ideas on what makes a good up tempo player.
[2022-01-30 16:24] action_jackson_123_fire : Cool. Sounds like there are many ways to evaluate players. Do a multitude of playing styles work assuming the parts fit together?
[2022-01-30 16:25] action_jackson_123_fire : Press, zone, up-tempo, slow, perimeter shooting etc?

[2022-02-01 20:02] Deleted User : My tactics is abysmal. What is the benefit of playing 50% zone and 50% man to man instead of the extremes?
[2022-02-02 00:09] elvira883 : Depends on your team. Man means they follow everyone around so they need to be good at both kinds of defense. Zone means they stay near their positions, which is better (and less tiring) for teams that have players with defense more suited to their position
[2022-02-02 00:51] furysk : man to man draws a lot of fouls, zone draws far fewer.
[2022-02-02 00:52] furysk : you might opt to 50/50 if you are trying to avoid pressure because the opponents overall passing/handling and their PG's passing/handling is to the point where you are likely to be burnt by pressure, but you want to also prevent your players from fouling out.

[2022-03-05 17:38] furysk : a bit late to this conversation, but i would offer a bit different an approach of any guys in theory can work, even at the cost of the punishment.
[2022-03-05 17:39] furysk : 5 stars are the least common scenario because the range of their potential and overalls usually lends itself to them being good enough in year 1 to play effectively.
[2022-03-05 17:43] furysk : For any other star there are two primary factors, SI and potential.  if the player in question has a gap of 65 between current projected true freshman starting SI and maximum SI it's a redshirt almost always.  if they gap is under 60 it's far more rare unless it's a 3 star and i'm trying to effectively keep my recruiting balanced.
[2022-03-05 17:47] furysk : most commonly, i've seen 3 star 10 potentials hitting 105-110 as a true freshmen in a few circumstances.  while it's plausible that they could go into the 11 potential range during development, i'm not actively that worried about them playing bench minutes and occasionally starting especially if they are a big as long as the height isn't slow to develop
[2022-03-05 17:48] furysk : i guess my point is, it's definitely not necessary to always redshirt and never redshirt specific setups.  perhaps the closest will be never redshirt 1 and 5 stars and just get them out, and most commonly redshirt 2 and 3, but you should always be adaptable to a specific players current value to your team and whether your team is in a position to either need the player to promote or need the player to stay up.

[2022-03-31 23:24] naph7777 : Here are all the evaluation comments ordered from "strongest" to "weakest" for each attribute.  IS - Could be a dominating post player IS - Could be a very good post player IS - Could be a good post player IS - Above average post moves  OS - Could be an excellent shooter OS - Could be a good shooter OS - Could be an above average shooter OS - Does not have much of a shooting touch  Rng - Could really be a long-range shooter  Reb - Can be a monster on the boards Reb - Can be a decent rebounder Reb - Can never be a good rebounder  ID/PD - Can be a great all-around defensive player ID/PD - good all-around defensive ID/PD - Will always be a poor defender PD - Will never be a good perimeter defender ID - Will never be a good interior defender  Note that "good all-around defensive" can be combined with a "never be" comment. Which means they will be really, really good at the other defensive attribute.
[2022-03-31 23:24] naph7777 : IQ - Can be a really smart player IQ - Can be a smart player IQ - Can be prone to a lot of mental mistakes  Pass - Can be a skilled passer with exceptional court vision Pass - Can be a skilled passer  Spd - Will be quick as lightning Spd - Will be very quick Spd - Can be a speedy player Spd - Will always be a bit sluggish  Hnd - Can be a really good ball handler Hnd - Can be a decent ball handler Hnd - Will be a below average ball handler  Other - Excellent all-around player Other - Good all-around player Other - Has no preference to play close to home Other - Would prefer to play close to home Other - Is a troubled kid and may not be college material (~50/50 of committing or never playing in colelege at the end of HS SR season) Other - Is eager to commit early (Will commit in first half of season if any contacts on them) Other - Isn't much of a student and may not qualify academically (~50/50 of committing or going to Junior College at end of HS SR season) Other - May choose to play overseas instead of going to college (International only - ~50/50 chance of committing or never playing in college.) Other - Will flourish in a fast pace offense Other - Will struggle in a fast pace offense Other - Will flourish in a slower tempo offense Other - Will struggle in a slower tempo offense Other - "Wants to commit on round XXX" - approximate wording  Things of note There are no evaluation comments for Finishing, Driving, Strength or Stamina There are no negative comments for Inside Shot, Range or Passing  Comments are not 100% accurate. (I've had a 19 IS "very good post player" and a capped out 15 IS "dominating post player")

[2022-04-01 00:00] rlawrenceune : i feel like i've been making assumptions for a long time now on what  a team need to play slow versus fast.  So, chime in o wise ones.  Slow versus fast, what skills does the team need?
[2022-04-01 00:04] fuzzy812 : slow needs passing and ball handling, fast needs speed
[2022-04-01 00:35] naph7777 : In general a slow team is trying to win by being more efficient. They will need more passing/IQ as they will make more passes than a team playing faster. Probably more handling too. They are likely to be able to get the ball to high efficiency inside players more often than a team that is pushing tempo. Slow team is going to want defenders who can force a low oFG%  In general a fast team is trying to win by generating more possessions, and trying to make some of those high efficiency transition baskets. They will benefit more from driving/handling/spd. Guards have the ball more often, when they are pushing the tempo they tend to take a higher percentage of the shots (so either throttle their green light, or recruit scorers appropriately). A fast team is going to want defenders than can force turnovers, as that fuels their transition.
[2022-04-01 00:36] naph7777 : Thats all my reasoning anyway.   I haven't been overly successful with tempo in HW IMO. I've won when I've out-talented teams, and generally lost when I haven't.
[2022-04-01 01:44] lynxvj : This is high quality info. Any chance you have something similar for coach comments?

I've seen 15 tactic coaches with no tactic related comment) 12-14 He is a good X's and O's coach. (This comment does not always appear) 0-11 (no comment)  Development 15+ He is excellent at teaching the game. 12-14 He is a good teacher of the game 9-11 (no comment) 0-8 He is a poor teacher of the game  Motivation 15+ He is a great motivator 12-14 He is a good motivator 0-11 (no comment)  Recruiting (Comment range before age starts to effect it) 15+ He is an excellent recruiter 13-14 He is a good recruiter. 11-12 He is a decent recruiter 5-10 (no comment, yes some go as low as 5 with no negative comment) 0-9 He is a poor recruiter (yes some stay as high as 9 with this negative comment)

[2022-04-03 23:57] furysk : on said recruiting page at the bottom it says 2/2 scholarships for next season, the following season is 0 - 3.
[2022-04-03 23:58] furysk : so you have two scholarships for this season meaning at most 2 guys will commit.  the 0 -3 means if you redshirt all juniors on your team you wont have a scholarship to use next season, if you redshirt none of them you have 3 available.  if you redshirt 1 or 2 you obviously have 2 or 1 open so it's just telling you the possible outcomes.
[2022-04-03 23:58] furysk : you use prospect search to find players.  local recruits are the easiest because state advantage in this game is super useful unless the player has "No preference to play close to home" in his scouting report on his page.
[2022-04-03 23:59] furysk : so setting it to Iowa in region, ticking uncommited prospects to a check mark position, and putting the class to Sr - Sr up top will show you everyone in Iowa that is still uncommitted to a school.
[2022-04-04 00:01] furysk : redshirts are just like that are in college basketball except more commonly used here.
[2022-04-04 00:03] furysk : if a player has less than 6 games played he can stop playing for the rest of the year, you can check them under game management options indicating you want them to sit out a season, and they can improve somewhere between 5 and 15 SI for the most part (there are some that go outside of this range but i'd say 95-98% of the players are in that range).  It's important when you have a player slightly behind in development because it gives them that extra time to get caught up and usable.
[2022-04-04 00:04] furysk : on your roster page, i was noting a few guys i would NOT redshirt.  Typically a player in D.VI has to be at 120-125 SI to be considered for a starting job if you want to be truly competitive to promote.  the game follows a pyramid structure to where the top 3 teams in each division promote up, the bottom 6 promote down, except in D.I where nobody promotes up and D.VI (your location) where there isn't anywhere to go down to so you can finish as low as you want and stay in there.

[2022-04-06 15:46] ablazemrglass : So the upper threshold and the lower threshold are the main cause of my confusion.
[2022-04-06 15:47] ablazemrglass : If I have an upper threshold up <10 for points in the paint does that mean my adjustments activate if my opponent scores more than 10 points in the paint? <@799707004335292467>
[2022-04-06 15:47] ablazemrglass : And it could be I'm just totally overthinking it... thank you
[2022-04-06 15:51] naph7777 : You are describing what condition you want your change in settings to occur. So in your example If you set an upper threshold of <= 10. With no lower threshold set. Then you are saying "if my opponent scores any number of points in the paint less than or equal to 10 then I want to use <some settings>"
[2022-04-06 15:52] naph7777 : Most of the instructions make more sense to set a lower threshold in my opinion.
[2022-04-06 15:53] naph7777 : "If opponent points in the paint - Lower Threshold >= (some number I decide means they are dominating the paint) then - Set Extend defense to -3"
[2022-04-06 15:54] naph7777 : "If opponent 3-pointers made - Lower Threshold >= 6 Then Set Extend Defense to +2"
[2022-04-06 15:54] naph7777 : Using the lower and upper threshold would be  more for things like. (Threshold Type = Point Differential) If we're down lots use this tactic (Lower Threshold = None + Upper threshold <=-20) If we're down a little use this tactic (Lower Threshold >= -19 + Upper Threshold <=-1) If we're up a little use this tactic (Lower Threshold >=0 + Upper Threshold <= 10) If we're up a lot use this tactic (Lower Threshold >=11 + Upper Threshold = None)
[2022-04-06 16:14] eljefe7705 : that would be less than 10 points as <@453580403366821899> said. If you want to trigger an adjustment to compensate for your opponent scoring a lot in the paint you would want to set the lower threshold to >=10 (or whatever number you're looking for - just make sure it's a positive number and not a negative)
[2022-04-06 16:16] ablazemrglass : Ahhhhh, that makes so much more sense. Thank you!
[2022-04-06 16:16] eljefe7705 : the adjustment you mentioned you could always consider using if you start the game with a tactic as a result of expecting the opponent to score a lot in the paint. So if they score fewer than 10 points in the paint, maybe you extend the defense a little bit more, or decide to play more man or zone
[2022-04-06 16:17] eljefe7705 : on the "down a little", "up a little" tactics that naph mentioned, you might decide that you don't want those triggered unless you're down by 5 points, or 7 points, etc. In that chase you would change the upper threshold to <=-5 (or -7) when "down a little" or >=5 (or 7) when "up a little"
[2022-04-06 16:18] eljefe7705 : that can be helpful when figuring out the sequence of your triggers
[2022-04-06 16:20] eljefe7705 : because the game engine will first look at adjustment 1; if that's not triggered it will go to adjustment 2.....etc. So what that means is if Adjustment 1 is Point Differential (Lower Threshold = None + Upper threshold <= 0) and Adjustment 2 is Point Differential (Lower Threshold >=1 + Upper Threshold = None), then Adjustments 3 through 5 will never be triggered because Adjustment 1 or 2 cover all scenarios whether you are winning or losing
[2022-04-06 16:22] eljefe7705 : so depending on your strategy, it could be helpful to prioritize Adjustments based on fouls, 3pts, points in the paint first and then point differential last............or set different types of thresholds on point differential so they're only triggered if you are winning or losing by a set amount (e.g., 5 points, 7 points, 10 points, etc)

[2022-04-23 12:37] c1458 : Is there a difference in recruiting benefit moving up divisions?

[2022-04-23 12:38] naph7777 : You can get a boost to recruit interest when you promote. You generally get more interest for less contacts in higher divisions.
[2022-04-23 12:38] naph7777 : I suspect the boost when you promote is simply the recruits interest being recalculated as if you had spent the same number of contacts at the higher division.
[2022-04-23 12:41] bergkamp7349 : somewhat yes. the biggest difference is between division 1 and 2 (LL4 and LL5)
[2022-04-23 12:47] c1458 : So once you get promoted to D1 is like the lowest division one then get promoted higher and higher?
[2022-04-23 12:49] naph7777 : All conferences starting with I, II, III, or IV are "D1".... V = D2, VI = D3.  I don't think I really understand the question you just asked.
[2022-04-23 13:46] slickandjakenillinois : Yes D1 is the best division, and you can continue getting promoted from Conference IV to III, then to Conference II, then to Conference I, aka Legends, all within D1.  Or conversely, you can also get demoted down Conferences if you finish bottom 6 of the conference, which includes getting demoted from IV to V which causes you to fall from D1 to D2.  There is a huge recruiting penalty on the D1 to D2 demotion on players you already have interest on, as well as requiring more contacts to get higher interest on players you start going after.  On the other hand, you get a boost on interest for recruits you already have interest on when promoting from D2 to D1.  There is a very minor boost, from my experience, when promoting within D1, such as from IV to III.  My promotion from IV to III saw none of my recruits change in interest at all, for example.  While my promotion from V to IV saw a boost on all of the recruits I already had interest on, and it was multiple sub levels.  For example, I had two guys on just HIGH who both went to Very High just with the promotion.

[2022-05-07 06:07] tps2.0. : I just finished an updated version for my recruiting tidbit I had, but it will be split up because of the character limit. Let me know about any mistakes, suggestions, and/or if it would be useful for a new player.
[2022-05-07 06:09] tps2.0. : 5. Recruiting redshirt penalties: If you recruit a four or five star you will have to decide if you are willing to take the risk of redshirting those player(s). On the one hand, redshirting them means you will get a premium player at the advanced stages of his development which will give you an advantage in his RS JR and SR years. It can also be useful if you have a SR/RS SR ahead of the recruit in question. A 170 SI upperclassmen will probably preform better than that prospect which would make a redshirt year an easier decision. The downside is the penalty that comes with it. After the redshirt year, it will be harder to recruit 4 and 5 stars to your team. If you plan on targeting those types of players, redshirting might not be as beneficial for you.
[2022-05-07 06:24] tps2.0. : 6. Negative comments: Sometimes a prospect will gain a troubled or academics(INTL prospects only come up for one year which means you immediately know about overseas) comment which is something out of our control. With that being said, it is important to still have a strategy for these guys. I'd personally rank these negative comments 1.  Isn't much of a student and may not qualify academically 2. May choose to play overseas instead of going to college 3. Is a troubled kid and may not be college material. An academics comment just means if the player doesn't commit he will go the JUCO route. It's a positive that you can still recruit that player. You will still have to battle for him while you lose two years the recruit is on your campus, but that junior college will still give your recruit a lot of minutes to develop. The INTL prospects who play overseas have one small advantage that I mentioned earlier. You will not be surprised by a sudden comment. You know coming into the INTL market who are the risks. Finally, those troubled recruits out there are all or nothing prospects that could get these comments as late as the flip before his senior year. These players will "disappear" if they do not commit. There is still a small advantage compared to the overseas prospects. If you are in-state or in-region, you usually have a small recruiting advantage. This means these recruits will take less contacts to reach the high interest level. All of this info is great, but you might want to know how we can use it to your advantage. Just like you, other presidents will be scared off on these prospects. There is still a chance you can take a risk depending on your scholarships. If you have one open scholarship, it might still be beneficial to see if the player ends up committing. I usually assume 50% of these recruits commit. This works really well with the INTL prospects since everyone will go after the sure things initially.
[2022-05-07 06:25] naph7777 : *redshirthing (this is a typo in section 5)
[2022-05-07 06:26] tps2.0. : 7. Location preference: I had a small comment on the actual location of a player, but not a comment. A recruit with the comment, "Would prefer to play close to home" will take less comments to recruit if you are in that recruits region. It's a relief if you are near the recruit and a nightmare if you aren't. It's also important to remember it applies to the universities and colleges in your state and region. You will get the same advantage/disadvantage as them. I use this comment to know how much of a lead I need. Funny enough I actually want more of a lead either way. Even though this comment usually takes out the out of region teams, it still means those schools close to me have the same advantage. They can catch up just as quick as me. I also want to make a quick note about how the comment works. Even though the comment makes the recruit easier to commit, it does not mean the player will commit to you just because you are in state. A recruit will still choose the out of region school on high even if you are an in-state school on low. This affects contacts not commitments. A player can also have the comment of , "Has no preference to play close to home". I read this as a level playing field. If this comment pops up late, it might not matter since most in-state and in-region schools will have invested in them, but it is good to know earlier. I treat these guys as INTL prospects where no one gets the location advantage. It is good to know that you don't have to worry as much as those pesky division 3 in-state schools.
[2022-05-07 06:26] tps2.0. : 8. Pace: I don't look at this too much, but if you plan on playing extremely fast or slow you want to play attention to this comment. As an example, I will pretend to manage a +5 team which means I want a fast offense. I'd want to try to avoid any prospects who struggle in my offense which is put "Will struggle in a fast pace offense". This shouldn't be a deal breaker(especially for 5 star prospects) but it could be a tie breaker. You do want to consider the recruits with the comment, "Will flourish in a fast pace offense". Once again, it isn't a deal maker, but consider it a tie breaker. These comments are similar for the slower offenses with fast being replaced with slow in the comment. Personally, I switch my offense tempo a lot, so I just take not of the struggle comments and put it with the rest of my evaluation of the prospect.
[2022-05-07 06:26] tps2.0. : 9. Attributes: Height is usually the most important one for good reason. You want your big men to be big. Some people also like their SF to also be big, but it is not as important in my opinion. It is important to remember that recruits will grow over three or four years and it will usually be around 6 to 8 inches. I don't usually look at projected height unless it is someone overseas. A current player of mine (http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/player/144562/A) initially came in at 6'6" with a 7' projected height. Since I didn't have a previous history of height (this is for all INTL ), I took a chance on him growing. At the time of this message, he grew three inches for me which puts him at PF territory for me. It also helped that I think he could play SF which rose his floor for me. I personally use 6'8" as a soft seperator but those other attributes can change that. A recruit with a high vertical and long wingspan can help some of those smaller players against the big boys. You can also get away with a smaller PF for the lower level teams out there(V and VI). I don't look at weight and shoots(what is their dominant hand) as much as other people). Age is the useless one since every player in each class is the same age. The INTL players are all the same age as the HS SR class. The only way I could ever see this being important in the future with the current format is if the pro level ever becomes playable which might give the 22 year old draft prospects an advantage over the 23 year old prospects. As mentioned earlier, this would give the pro teams an extra year since most players come into the league pretty much developed.
[2022-05-07 06:31] naph7777 : Section 7: "I had a small comment on the actual location of a player, but not a comment. " - I don't understand what you are trying to say with this sentence.
[2022-05-07 06:36] tps2.0. : I did have to cut that one down due to character limits. I might go back to make 7. sound smoother.
[2022-05-07 06:40] naph7777 : The rest of it reads well. It contains generally agreed upon information, and includes some of your own preferences/opinions which is fine.

[2022-06-11 00:05] furysk : My philosophy on coaches ahs always been this: Recruiting - overrated if you are mostly on smaller targets, so it's only important to be 'neutral' in the VI-V climbs where your targets shouldn't for the most part be major investments.  you wont get enough value on 10 contacts from a 20 recruiting head coach, but you might get some reasonable value on 100 contacts from 20 recruiting  Development - Doesn't change too much from the base value of prospects, so if you are investing in 115-120 SI 11 potentials this isn't as important, but it can definitely improve your pace of development enough to not take too many poor coaches in that field.  Offense/Defense/Tactics - if you have roughly neutral overall (1 positive 1 negative 1 nothing) you generally wont see enough of an impact to merit worrying about it.  all negative or all positive should in theory give you a small boost, but i've not seen a reasonable amount of proof at this point to think that it amounts to much more than a bucket or so against an average coach and 2 or 3 if the other coach is garbage and detrimental.    Motivation - Again, i think if an average motivation has 5 minute swings of poor shooting + opponent shoots well, then below average is 6 minutes and above average is 4.  This is probably only impactful in my mind when the differences are more than 10 between coaches AND talent is equal AND the tempo dictates that the possesions that occur within a minute are enough to give 3 looks at the basket during it.

[2022-06-27 18:08] slickandjakenillinois : I think this nails a big part of it, especially offensive fouls (which I think also depends on other factors too).  I have seen bugs get a lot of over the back rebounding fouls, which depends on certain skill differences between the players going for the rebound.  But on the defensive end, I think it depends on a lot of factors.  Player size/build who they are matched against, certain differences in skill as well, but even for big men how good your perimeter defenders are.  If the opponent has guards driving successfully all the time, it increases the chances of your bigs getting fouls (and blocks) not only on the penetrating guard, but potentially on the player he may dish to at the basket.  So if a team is causing your bigs to foul a lot by penetrating, then that means not only are they exploiting a weakness of yours, but also as a player you need to adapt your defensive tactics to compensate (and potentially opening yourself up to other ways to be attacked on that end).  When it comes down to it, I feel player skills make the biggest difference.  However, there are also games where your players just play bad.  That happens on real life too.  Don’t let one off games skew your understanding or perception of the game.
[2022-06-27 18:29] david118242 : That's an interesting point on the driving guards and makes sense. You see that all the time in real games where a guard gets beat and a big has to step out and challenge but depending on their speed or IQ aren't suited to it.

[2022-08-07 23:37] aj22222. : I need some lineup advice for army, we are on a 3 game losing streak and now In the regulation zone. What would you have army's lineup looking like in my situation. Thank you in advance
[2022-08-08 01:34] naph7777 : I think your depth chart looks largely fine to me. That said, I'd play Carey at bPG because I think you should develop him and he's your 2nd best IQ/Pass/Hnd guy. I'd be hiding Cannon on whicher position is weakest between bSG/bSF/bPF. Frazier the next weakest. Worthington to play bC and either bPF or bSF. He'd definitely be my bSF against some of the higher scoring SF's in your conference.  Frazier's 3-ball isn't dropping this year. Should probably be on " " for offensive positioning, which let him take more mid-range shots and probably use his finishing a little more.  Jeter & Bello are both better from 2 than 3. Would set each of them 1 more step towards "I".  You have small rebounding and turnover advantages, but are losing in eFG%. Against any team you think you will out-rebound I'd be pushing the tempo. Against the top teams, you probably want a bit slower and hope that RNG works out in your favour, and it should keep the overall score (and hopefully margin) down. In general you're pretty deep, so a faster game should suit you more often.  On defense I'm guessing you are somewhere near the middle for extension. I think you probably need to try harder to take something away from your opponent. More often than not I try and make the 2FG's harder as they take more of them (so -2 or -3 on extension). Especially if you are down at half time, try something more extreme to take something away. If your opponent goes the wrong way and focuses where your defense is, you might win some games you otherwise wouldn't. If you know they are going to jack a tonne of 3's (MMA for example) then maybe go +2 or +3.  You're late enough in the season that your Green Light should be more set on players eFG% or TS% than their attributes. Feed the guys who have been efficient (Luce & Egan), throttle down the less efficient guys (Frazier, Worthington, Cannon)

[2022-10-19 14:00] naph7777 : I think there is an argument that you could swap out Malik Ross for a development/recruiting coach. Carlin your current head coach is getting old, but is an elite recruiter, and decent elsewhere so I'd probably keep him on a bit longer. Meade has nice some nice strengths that compliment Carlin. But he's 48. When he turns 51 he will leave to become a head coach elsewhere, so you need to make a decision on whether to make him your head coach soon, or to move on.  As for when it happens. The greatest number of coaches are available during the season flip. It is first in, first served, so you just have to be online at the magic time, and be quick with your decisions. So you probably want to decide on skills/age you would accept. It can be done for quite a while after that, but all of the best coaches will go in a matter of minutes.

[2022-12-16 05:22] rhinolewis : what is the difference between motivation and development (for coaches) in terms of what happens to your team in terms of one or the other
[2022-12-16 05:22] rhinolewis : ?
[2022-12-16 05:29] mdoman12 : Motivation: how well can the coach motivate the team such that and control and cope with swings in game momentum.
[2022-12-16 05:30] mdoman12 : Development: how well does the coach develops young players.
[2022-12-16 05:31] mdoman12 : So motivation is for in game. If your coach is a good motivator your team could respond really well when the other team goes on a run. Bad motivator could mean your team giving up when the other team gets a lead.
[2022-12-16 05:31] mdoman12 : Development is more so how well your players progress

[2022-12-16 14:15] slickandjakenillinois : I can account for about 80-85% of player development through a few variables.  Knowing this I then gathered data from many different players where the head coach development ranged from 0-20.  The data did not return any statistical significance in the player development at all attributed to the coach development rating, and 80-85% of the player development were still from the previous variables identified.  Perhaps there may be some error in the measurement if the coach development rating I was using was still not revealing the actual rating.  Or that I included Freshmen and Sophomores versus just freshmen.  Or that I did not account for assistant coach development ratings (does poor assistant coach ratings HURT development???).  Or perhaps something else I am not accounting for that skews the data.  But ultimately I would still think there would be some correlation seen, and therefore my conclusion is the vast majority of player development comes from variables other than head coach development rating.

[2023-01-04 14:54] bridger29 : *"My strategy is generally to recruit 2 or 3 players each season. Its lead to very steady results, but perhaps I should look at a less balanced approach to give me more promotion/tournament chances? (I've only had 5 D1 tournament appearances R64x2, R32x2, R8x1)"*  This part is interesting and relatable.  I went with a very unbalanced recruiting cycle for a long time intentionally.  I think it was 6-4-2-1-0.  This led to some very strong "peak" seasons (6 seniors, 4 juniors!!) and some very poor "down" seasons (1 senior, 0 juniors!!).  I was able to climb doing this because I usually only demoted once per cycle and could often promote 2-3 times per cycle.  I have shifted over the last 5+ seasons to recruiting 2-3 players each season because I am trying to have a sustained run in the top leagues.  I think if you are looking to climb up to the top from the lower leagues, there are definitely some advantages to imbalanced recruiting cycles but it comes with a cost.
[2023-01-04 14:57] bridger29 : All that said, the best strategy is probably to not get locked into a particular cycle and to instead target players that fit your strategy and look to spend points intelligently (i.e. avoid battles, target undervalued profiles, etc.).  I like to plan out long-term and recruit ahead, so I miss lots of opportunities for value.

[2023-05-07 12:17] naph7777 : In my opinion it pays to go hard on players. You goal should be to go from None to at least Medium and preferably High interest in 1 day on a player that nobody else is showing interest on. If its later in the recruiting cycle, maybe you go to Med/High on someone who is showing Low interest in another team.  What you don't do is limp to Low interest on a number of recruits, then keep giving them all 1 contact occasionally.
[2023-05-07 12:18] dimbity : so like wht the ai did hehe
[2023-05-07 12:18] naph7777 : In your early days you spread things around a little as you work out what your range is for getting a recruit to Low interest.
[2023-05-07 12:20] naph7777 : Even on guys in region there will be some variance. Some guys might go to Low interest for 4 contacts, some 5 or 6, maybe some might even go for 3 contacts. Its going to take 7 times that many contact (often a few more on top of that) to get them to High interest. So whether it take them 4 or 6 or 8 contacts makes a big difference on your total spend.

[2023-05-07 12:23] dimbity : oooo i see lol
[2023-05-07 12:23] naph7777 : The only risk of keeping a scholarship offer on a player is that you might sign them. So the only time I pull scholarships is when I don't want that player. Maybe I did want them, but I've signed another player at their position. Or I've changed plans for some other reason... or maybe they looked good as a freshman, but now they are a senior and they haven't developed as I hoped they would. That sort of thing.  Its very rare though. Contacts are precious. Even a very small chance of signing someone of value is better than no chance.

Best case with promoting is you somehow find a way to stay up and you gain all the recruiting benefits. What's the best case with not promoting?

[2023-06-02 02:55] naph7777 : I get the best head coach I can (total skills, leaning towards recruiting and development) Then I want to find an assistant who will be my future head coach. So either sign a good coach of assistant age, OR take a chance on young coaches with no reputation and hope to get lucky that one of them becomes my future head coach. Then after I have those 2 locked away, then I'm looking for complementary coaches. That normally means an assistant who has a strength where my top 2 coaches have a weakness. eg http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/coaches/65 Finch is the had coach. Scales is the head-coach-in-waiting. Then I got Jorgensen as an Off/Mot guy, and after that I got Flaherty who turned into a really good Mot/Rec guy.
[2023-06-02 02:59] naph7777 : Keep in mind that there are limits so you can only sign 1 coach per day I think it is. So as a new team. Grab a great coach if you're lucky enough to be online for the coach feeding frenzy. But in all likelihood, I'd be looking to grab young coaches who have most skills in the 10-12 range with either no, or undeveloped reputations (see the pinned post in this channel for all the coach comments), and keep cycling through them until you get a good one to be your future head coach.

I recommend not taking on too many recruiting battles as an LL6 team

[2023-06-09 14:37] chousley4 : One of the things I love about hardwood is that you can build very competitive teams from almost every single state. You don’t really have to go out of your state to be a winning program. If you look at the top players or the draft there are so many 2 and 3 star guys that develop into studs.   - Find guys you like in your state and get them.  - fill in your roster with slightly under recruited guys in your region.   And you’ll have a good enough team to enjoy the game long enough to start building a competitive program.
[2023-06-09 15:40] cdilks : Points are points regardless of when you use them, so I don’t think you should ever feel bad going after someone that has already been contacted. That said, I think you generally get better value going after someone with no interest, because if you build a lead, it might scare other people off(Depending on the player. For a top player, I’d always assume someone else is going to Very High on them)
[2023-06-09 15:40] cdilks : I’d try to avoid expensive head-to-head battles early on. I just don’t think any single player is worth it at that point.
[2023-06-09 15:41] cdilks : Going out-of-region is really only for when you’re desperate later in a recruiting cycle and are looking for someone that hasn’t been contacted yet.It’s extremely difficult to win a head-to-head battle with someone in-region that wants that player and probably not the best use of your points.
[2023-06-09 15:41] cdilks : I think new users tend to aim too high with their recruiting. You don’t need high-end players to be successful. The goal should be to find guys that are in the sweet spot of not quite being developed enough for a D1 team to take, but someone that is going to turn into a good player with the gobs of playing time you have available. Something like 80-90SI as a HS SR(70+ for anyone taller than 6’9”) with good potential.
[2023-06-09 15:48] dimbity : I still trying to learn what's good hehe and balancing comments  and current attys
[2023-06-09 20:23] furysk : i agree with most of what cdilks says above.  When you have a lot of spots to fill, and you have nobody recruited out in the Junior and Sophomore classes, you first need to get to the point where you are ahead enough to do that.  So chasing some guy that is on high with some other team, especially if the other team is in state or in region and you are new, is a bad idea period.  Newer players don't fully grasp what spending needs to happen to get to that point, and you can't see if the other team has a player on very high or not, so you have to keep spending to give yourself the best chance.  just becomes prohibitive towards getting ahead in recruiting in a hurry.
[2023-06-09 20:25] furysk : At the end of season, i tend to look around at guys that haven't committed to single teams with medium/high interest, as quite a few teams recruit +1 player (meaning they offer past their scholarship count by 1.  so if they have 2 scholarships, they invest contacts and offer to 3).  You can sneak some guys that are better than the no interest guys sometimes.
[2023-06-09 20:27] furysk : i set limits on the top talents mentally that i think i need to spend, and just head to that number asap.  So if a guy is critical to my team, i'll spend 25+25+40+60 systematically to give myself a good chance against 99% of the teams out there recruiting as not too many will go beyond 150 contacts.

[2023-07-07 02:01] lassoball : The answer truly is “it depends”.    It depends on position.  You can reach more on a low SI big, provided they are tall/going to be tall and have the right build (IS/REB/ID/etc)  It also depends on POT and growth curve.  I’ll reach more for a 12 POT+ and/or if they’ve already demonstrated a good growth curve.  The difference in recruiting an 80 SI junior that started as a 60 vs a 30 is massive in terms of future trajectory.  When it comes to day 1 freshmen, I try to ask myself whether I would be happy committing as a SR with 40-45 more SI than they have currently and a build consistent with their comments.    Hard to throw out a hard number (others may have one), but hope that helps

[2023-07-27 07:32] naph7777 : In order of priority: 1) Find your next head coach * Sign a guy who's good enough and young enough * OR, someone who already looks like they will grow enough (already has positive comments) * OR, sign fresh all-10's guy and hope to get lucky. 2) Once you have your next head coach lined up. [2023-07-29 12:45] fatherborf : followup cuz this has confused me: how does coach skill growth work? every ("every" lol, all 3 of them) off-season when i peruse to see if theres someone worth picking up, i notice there are a lot of 30 something coaches at all 10s, and then there are the ACs with "actual" skill distributions, usually 40+. how does the former group become the latter group? do the skills actually change/grow in their 30s, or is it an extension of what you said about displayed ratings, when they are young the displayed ratings are inaccurate and they simply display more accurate numbers over time?
[2023-07-29 12:47] fatherborf : i thought initially it would be kind of cool to have a whole coaching staff "start" their careers on a team around the same time but was terrified that hiring 3 all 9/10 thirty year old ACs meant theyd never change from that
[2023-07-29 12:48] fatherborf : these guys
[2023-07-29 14:31] naph7777 : 1) Coaches have a final rating (well, final before they decline due to old age) 2) Coaches start with most (often all) skills displaying as 10's 3) Slowly over time the 10's move towards their final ratings. 4) At some stage after the ratings start moving, some of the coaching attributes get an intermediate reputation comment. 5) At a later stage even more coaching attributes get a final reputation comment. (Replacing the intermediate comment)  It is possible that the rating they are moving towards changes over time. But I don't think it really matters one way or another.  If you scroll through the pinned posts in this channel, or search it for "Coaching Comment Ranges" you can see the ranges that each comment (or lack of comment) can be for a coaches final attribute.
[2023-07-29 14:32] fatherborf : okay thank you so much, that makes a lot of sense. maybe ill replace a somewhat mediocre AC turning 50 next season with a young coach just for the fun of seeing them develop for a while
[2023-07-29 14:34] naph7777 : You can always just browse through some assistant coaches that aren't all 10's. You'll get a feel for how many seasons they need to have coached to move to having 5's and 15's for example. The info is there if you want it and don't want to wait multiple seasons to get it.
[2023-07-29 14:35] naph7777 : This is easier if you check the "Include Coaches under contract" checkbox. Look at young coaches that have moved a lot from all 10's. Then you'll get an even better idea of what a good coach looks like at a young age. So you'll know who to stick with, and who to move on.
[2023-07-29 14:55] fatherborf : oh yeah thats an excellent idea, thanks for that tip thats much easier

[2023-07-30 13:05] tavessoul : Just my two cents on why I voted yes, but first a disclaimer:  I've never red-shirted a 5-star, only 4-stars.  So, I'm guessing a little that the penalties are similar, with obviously more weight for doing it with a 5-star. For me there are three questions here: 1) **Does redshirting him hurt you for future recruits that much?**  My experience with the 4-star penalty was that it mainly affected other 4 and 5-star prospects, and that it stacks if you're doing it with multiple 4 or 5-stars. Since SMC only really has one 5-star target in it's sites, and he's going to committ this year it seems like the affect shouldn't be too bad.  I do think there's a realistic chance if you got Burgess he'd have to redshirt too, but maybe not. 2) **Do you need him to fill a spot in the rotation this season?**  You've got Z-Bit, Cha Cha, Horse, Dingo and Hassle all ready to eat those minutes at the 3/4/5 spots, so you don't need him.  There's no pressing spot in the rotation, and he's not changing your size equation in most situations. 3) **Does playing him help SMC this season?**  As you mentioned above, you don't need him.  You've got guys who should be eating those minutes, who are better players at the moment.  Prioritizing his minutes could end up costing you some tight games.  So, because I don't think it hurts you that much, and doesn't really help you this season at all, I went with yes, redshirt him.

[2023-08-06 06:57] adrian_toth : Can I have your advice on pace? With what type of team would you play more up-tempo and play slower pace? [2023-08-06 13:21] naph7777 : __Things that make me play faster__ * My team is overall better than my opponent * I am likely to win the possession battle (more rebounds, fewer turnovers) * My team has high stamina * My team has a lot of depth * I want to concentrate shots on my guards * My team has important players that will flourish in a fast offense, or struggle in a slow offense   __Things that make me play slower__ * My team is overall worse than my opponent * I am likely to lose the possession battle (particularly if I think my team can be more efficient shooting the ball - ie my eFG% / oeFG% margin is better than opponent) * My team has low stamina * I'm running a short rotation * Want to get more shots for my bigs * My team has important players that will flourish in a slow offense, or struggle in a fast offense
[2023-08-06 13:53] _plokmijn : Naph said it all, but adding to point 2 for playing slower, I usually play slower if my team is a lot better defensively than it is offensively. Slow pace gives my team a chance to keep up scoring wise. On the other hand, it’s almost always better to play fast if your team has an awesome offense with lots of scoring options

[2023-08-22 23:02] naph7777 : This is why PD is better on your SF's than ID. They'll do better in a zone. Due to the default zone that is used.

[2023-10-27 18:31] bridger29 : https://tenor.com/view/joke-jk-penguin-laugh-its-was-a-joke-gif-14574338
[2023-10-29 06:48] adrian_toth : Can somebody please give me some advice on when to use more zone, when to use more man-to-man defense?
[2023-10-29 12:53] bridger29 : There are lots of different ways people determine the importance of these two.  Some think zone is more effective vs inside offense and man vs outside...not everyone agrees with that.
[2023-10-29 12:54] bridger29 : Another way to look at is to look at individual matchups of your starters vs theirs.  If all of the defensive matchups look good, then more man makes sense.  If you have a weak spot or two, maybe zone helps avoid isolating those matchups.
[2023-10-29 12:55] bridger29 : Some think that man creates more fouls, so if you are worried about foul trouble in a matchup or can't afford a few key players getting into foul trouble, more zone may make sense.
[2023-10-29 12:55] bridger29 : But at the end of the day, each team and each season is different, so you have to experiment with your team and see what's working vs different things and figure out the best plan for you!  There is no magic formula that you can just plug in each game and suddenly see consistent results.
[2023-10-29 12:56] naph7777 : Its even harder because the pros and cons of man versus zone are debated at lots of different levels.... And you basically have to guess what Steve thinks the advantages/disadvantages of each are.... and he hasn't told us what he thinks.
[2023-10-29 12:57] bridger29 : The one thing Steve has told us is that "Zone" is a 3-2 zone, which means the SF will likely play more perimeter defense than interior defense when you are in zone, so do with that what you will!
[2023-10-29 12:59] naph7777 : This is one of the reason ECU are playing mostly Man this year. Their SF has more ID than PD. I don't want him on the perimeter more than he has to be.
[2023-10-29 14:19] _plokmijn : Man: - Heavily rewards teams with size and speed  - Defender positioning is more based on the offensive positioning of their matchup (need more well rounded defenders for switches) - Good for sticking best defenders on strongest scorers, or hiding weak defenders on bad scorers (need players with positional versatility)  - More susceptible to slashers and elite scoring bigs  Zone: - Good option for teams with perimeter players lacking speed - Relies heavily on having strong ID and rebounding from your bigs (creates less turnovers, need to get the ball back when they miss) - Defensive positioning is more defined (players with very unbalanced defensive rating stay where they are best at) - Not as effective against teams with an elite PG (or multiple players with high IQ and passing) - Causes less fatigue (can help balance out high pressure or fast paced offense)
[2023-10-29 14:20] _plokmijn : A lot more to both defenses, but just a couple quick thoughts I have on each
[2023-10-29 17:50] adrian_toth : Wow, thank you guys! These are incredibly helpful and detailed! I definitely save these among my notes on how to play hardwood
[2023-10-29 17:53] eljefe7705 : I would recommend keeping in mind that these are basic principles of zone. I've had teams that should be good at man but are better at zone and vice versa, so a lot of it is finding the right balance for your team mix during non-con

[2023-11-03 18:07] juema : What's the chance of recruiting a player with the academic comment? I've never tried before and I don't know if it's worth it.
[2023-11-03 18:28] lassoball : Some say 50/50* they commit to a team, some say less.  The main thing to know is that player will go to JuCo if he doesn’t commit, as opposed to the “troubled kid” comment where they disappear from the game entirely and canonically start working in a shoe store.     It comes down to a holistic judgement really: Are there comparable prospects without academic issues? Is there competition on the player? If he goes to junior college, are you willing to re-offer him the scholarship as a JuCo and potentially put more contacts into him to have him play two seasons?  *Referring to odds at start of senior season.  If you are looking at a senior with that comment now in this stage of the recruiting cycle, it’s considerably more likely they are not going to commit. Exception is if nobody has offered him a scholarship yet, in which case he likely has his initial, start of season odds.

[2023-12-08 01:45] naph7777 : __Depth Chart__ I think you have your starting 5 right.  Kerr / Woods / Childers / Lawton / Jacobsen  Its a bit undersized, but not horribly so. It really struggles for passing, but that's the entire roster, not just your starters.  For the bench I'd have: Morris / Marte / Shepherd / Burns / Bowers  Ideally you probably should have redshirted Burns this year, which would have made space for Bolin. Bolin probably is your best big off the bench, and his passing could help, but I personally wouldn't be starting a 128 SI RS SR over FR/RS-FR that aren't that much worse. If you want to maximise winning this year, then sure, keep Bolin at bPF/bC, and Burns/Bowers will just get scraps, but it will hurt the long term development of Burns/Bowers.  I think Morris has to be the bPG even though his defense is so bad. 8 passing is pretty good for your team, he has the best handle on the bench. A season or 2 from now he could be 12/16 pass/handle with 12 OS. None of your other options look like they will get enough passing IMO.   __Strengths__ Kerr's a decent PG, at least on offense. Lawton is a good PF. Overall you have decent handles and IQ. Pretty good speed on your starters. Okay OS/Fin/Drv/Str on your starters.  __Weaknesses__ Really bad perimeter defending. Bad passing. Stamina's not great. Not much inside scoring.   __Tempo__ So you have a starter that is bad at a fast tempo, and one of your 2 best players has low stamina. That's definitely pushing you towards a slower tempo. But your passing is really bad, so if you slow it down too much, you'll just throw the ball away. So I'd probably start at -2 or -3, and see how bad the turnovers are, may well end up at -1 or 0.
[2023-12-08 01:45] naph7777 : __Defense__ I don't think you have the PD, depth or stamina for pressing. So I'd be 0-10% pressure.  Would probably lean more towards Zone. You'll get burnt from outside anyway, but at least you'll keep your passable ID guys and rebounders near the basket more often. May well just mix it up and go half zone, half man. I don't think it matters in the sim, but at least in theory you're giving your opponent different looks.  I'd probably experiment with 0 to -3 or -4 extension on defense. If a team gets hot from three you will lose, but trying to extend the defense out with your PD won't stop them anyway, and at least you'll make teams work for their 2FG.
