[2023-12-12 06:18] yessirr227 : Could someone break down the different "substitution modes" in the tactics
[2023-12-12 07:33] naph7777 : A - you might use this if you have 5 starters, and 5 backups each backing up a different position B -  you might instead use this if you have 5 starters, and 5 backups each backing up a different position C - as you don’t qualify for A or B you will be using this.
[2023-12-12 10:22] naph7777 : Alright that's probably a bit flippant.... here's the long version.   Mass Substitution     All positions: minutes 7-15  All 5 bench players will be on the court at the same time. Having a starter as a reserve at a 2nd position might work, but will result in them playing 15 minutes straight, so I hope they bring stamina. Generally works best if you want all your starters to only play together and all your bench players to play together. If you want that, I have to ask... Are you sure you want that?   Staggered Substitution A (the original)     C: minutes (remaining in the half) 18-11     PG & SF: minutes 15-8     SG & PF: minutes 12-5  Should be good for a PF/bC (ie hiding a lack of bC, getting a bPF to play more mins). Could also be good for a SG/bPG, SG/bSF or PF/bSF, again allowing more minutes for a bench player at SG or PF, whilst hiding a lack of bPG or bSF.    Staggered Substitution B (best pattern to have "key" positions filled with optimal players)     PG & C: minutes 18-11     SG & PF: minutes 12-5     SF: minutes 15-8  Good for a SG/bPG or a PF/bC. Could be okay for a SF/bSG or SF/bPF.   Staggered Substitution C (shorter bench periods)     C: minutes 18-15 & 12-9     PF: minutes 15-12 & 6-3     SF: minutes 12-6     SG: minutes 18-15 & 6-3     PG: minutes 15-12 & 9-6  Subbing all over the place. I think this generally works best if your depth chart doesn't nicely match up for A or B. Trying to play a 6th man starter minutes at 3 positions? You want C. Trying to make sure you don't have long stretches with mostly bench players in? You want C.   I almost exclusively use C. Though I should probably think about it a bit more often than I do as occasionally A or B could be good.

[2024-02-08 15:52] gards710 : that's a fantastic question! I certainly don't know the answer. I think when the player is set to o or O, it is both spacing and shot selection. But I? [2024-02-08 15:56] naph7777 : I think its most likely a distribution. " " for a SF might be 25/25/25/25 (Post/Drive/Jump-shot/3-pointer), switch it to "i" and maybe its 30/35/25/15 I think there's probably a different default distribution for each position, which makes it even harder to work out if that's how it works.  And to muddy the waters even further, there seems to be some sort of player-tendency factor as well. [2024-02-08 15:58] zyarbs1 : *game manual*  determines where a player tends to play on offense. Perimeter positions (PG, SG & SF) with an inside selection will tend to slash to the basket and in some cases post up their defenders. With an outside selection, they will tend to remain on the perimeter and launch long distance shots. An intermediate selection will result in more balanced play with mostly setting up on perimeter, but some forays towards the basket. Similarly, big men (PF & C) with outside selections will tend to favor moving outside of the paint and exercising their jump shot. An intermediate or inside selection will instruct the player to work inside the paint. Please note, these setting will affect where a player gets the ball and shoots/drives from, but will also have some affect also on his offensive rebounding position as well.
[2024-02-08 15:58] naph7777 : * note I have no idea if it is 25/25/25/25, I'm just throwing some numbers out there. I don't think SF's actually post up 25% of the time.
[2024-02-08 16:00] gards710 : well there ya go, the game manual DOES have the answer! Blackbeard can't complain about that
[2024-02-08 16:00] zyarbs1 : The way I’ve taken it is that the position being played is the most important factor for where a player will take most of their shots. A sg on “o” and a pf on “o” will take very different shots throughout the season.

[2024-03-07 20:24] bsmall84 : anybody have advice on player management settings. Any parameters or stats to look at to determine GL, offense positioning, and hook?
[2024-03-07 20:34] gards710 : with green light, it's a whole bunch of things and also feel. Size (height and weight) is important. I'd say OS + IS/RNG (depends on their position and where you position them), Fin, IQ, HNDL, DRV, Speed, Strength, and Stamina are all important. Driving is less important for a post big, but even for a guy who only shoots 3s, having it helps them not be one-dimensional and easier to stop. And sometimes, even if they have good ratings in all that, they just don't score how you think they should. As you've probably experienced in your many seasons, some guys just shoot more (and some less) than others, whether that's bc of position or some "hidden" personality/DNA thing, we don't know. But take all of that into account. One thing I'd look at and consider is their points per possession - if it's really high (like 1.1+), then consider giving them more of a green light. But you have to balance that with the thought that maybe they're better/more efficient at that lower usage.   For offensive positioning, a lot is based on position inherently. But look at which way the player's ratings tilt - an inside scoring guard would like something like 10/13/6/13. But you also should consider the player's handling, IQ, speed, and driving. If they can't get to the bucket, it doesn't matter, you know? An outside shooting big is really more just a question of if their RNG > IS enough and if you want to pull them out of chances for offensive rebounds.  Hook: look at how often they were DQ'd. This simply has a lot to do with the minutes tbh. Ratings-wise, I'd say the relevant defensive stat (perimD for perimeter guys, intD for bigs) and IQ. But also speed and IQ will play roles.
[2024-03-07 21:21] stromstar : I think each player has a bit of an x-factor as well

[2024-03-14 11:48] lynxvj : Do you adjust your defense extension based on your defensive strength? For example, if your team PD is slightly weaker, then you extend more?
[2024-03-14 11:52] _plokmijn : I use it as a starting point for my default tactics and then adjust up or down based on the opponents offensive strengths
[2024-03-14 11:59] lynxvj : How big of a difference between avg  PD and ID when you start adjusting the extension slider? I assume if the diffs is only abt 2-3 points, you just use neutral as default, right?
[2024-03-14 12:46] _plokmijn : Yeah if at about 3 points difference I’d start letting the skill difference dictate the defensive setting, anything less and I’d just go with whatever defensive philosophy you’d like to implement
[2024-03-14 12:50] lynxvj : Great. Thanks for your insight.
[2024-03-14 14:43] naph7777 : Interesting topic. I'm really curious how people work out their defensive settings. Extension Zone Press
[2024-03-14 14:46] mdoman12 : Before the season I set my tactics based on strengths of my team. Day-to-day I adjust slightly based on the starters of the team I’m playing. (Also how I usually set my green lights and offensive positioning as well)
[2024-03-14 14:47] naph7777 : I base my Zone/Man based on whether I feel like my guys are switchable or not (guys with closer to even ID/PD split are more switchable), guys who are taller are generally more switchable.  Pretty much base extension on my opponent, and not related to my team. Press goes down if my opponent has great overall hands/passing. Goes up if they have none. Generally defaults fairly low. If i have bad defense, but decent length/speed then I've pressed more with that too.
[2024-03-14 14:59] poletz : What i still didn t get is this: Extended defence makes the opponent take less 3pts shots, or diminish their efficiency, or both. ?
[2024-03-14 14:59] poletz : For marking i m on 100% zone since 2 seasons now with quite decent results 😁
[2024-03-14 14:59] naph7777 : Probably both.
[2024-03-14 15:03] naph7777 : Things I would expect it to do 1) More pressure on ball-carriers (more turnovers on opponent guards) 2) Harder to pass on the perimeter (more turnovers for perimeter focused offenses) 3) Give up more drives -> more fouls on defensive bigs. Give up more easy buckets inside 4) More space on the inside for post ups. 5) Lowers o3FG%, raises o2FG% 6) Lowers o3PA, raises o2PA
[2024-03-14 15:16] lynxvj : For me, if my team is overall bad defensively, then I run more zone. The extension setting is if there's pronounced differences in PD / ID. Unsure about press. I guess you can press more if your opp PGs are bad, but that's seldom seen in D1.
[2024-03-14 15:30] mdoman12 : I like the strategy of retracting the defense when you have good PD guards as that will offset closing the defense in, while simultaneously  helping your teams ID. Flipped if your defensive strength is the interior.

[2024-03-15 10:54] chrism3598 : Recruiting question - as a terrible team (i.e, #845), I've taken what I consider to be a pretty defensive approach to recruiting - basically bottom fishing and avoiding any bidding wars. Or does it just take a lot fewer recruiting points for a rank 45 team to get to medium interest than it would take me at 850 to get the same recuit to medium interest?
[2024-03-15 11:56] _plokmijn : It’s closer to the second one. Team prestige, league level, RS history, and current roster status all play into how much interest a recruit has in a school. If you are on high and other teams are on medium, you have the best chance of signing the player regardless of team ranking.
[2024-03-15 11:57] naph7777 : Phrased another way. It will take you more recruiting points to get a given recruit to High interest than it will for a "better" team. That's their advantage. But as plokmijn said. If you're on High and they are on Medium. You've got the inside lane and will win way more often than not.

[2024-04-26 14:26] cdilks : https://tenor.com/view/well-youre-half-wrong-doodybeard-is-not-quite-wrong-is-not-totally-wrong-its-half-half-gif-21057609
[2024-04-26 14:44] cdilks : I think what most people do is look at scouting reports for traits that match what they want for certain positions(Don't pay any attention to a player's HS position. You can convert them to a position in college.) So for a PG: SPD, HND, Pass, IQ, PDef are usually the big priorities. C/PF, you're usually looking for IS, Reb, IDef, Str. Shooting guard: SPD, either good OS/Rng or Drv/Fin, PDef. Small forward: Probably the most flexible position. Ideally someone that can do a little bit of everything.
[2024-04-26 14:50] cdilks : There's also a relationship between size and skill as gards mentioned. It's probably not 50/50, but being bigger than your opponent can mitigate some skill gap. My unscientific best guess at what constitutes average size for each position(at least for D1, lower levels tend to have smaller C/PF) PG: 6'1" SG: 6'3" SF: 6'5" PF: 6'8" C: 6'10
[2024-04-26 14:54] eljefe7705 : i'm sure someone could figure out the weighting of height/SI if they were willing to spend the time digesting the historical draft positions of bigs compared to guards
[2024-04-26 14:54] eljefe7705 : *someone smarter than me
[2024-04-26 15:02] cdilks : And like everything else in the game, there's a lot of variance built in. I play a ton of match-ups where I'm +4" in height/-40 in SI and sometimes it goes very well, sometimes I get eaten alive.
[2024-04-26 15:12] eljefe7705 : and sometimes you win a natty

[2024-05-19 13:40] thewhitehope : I was curious and maybe this isn't the right spot but wasn't sure where to ask. Anyway, the question is about the IS OS and Range. So let's say you have a player with low IS and low range. So maybe a range of like 4 or 5. But his OS is like a 12. What does his game look like?  I guess he can't shoot 3's well cause his range is short?  Maybe he's what shooting a bunch of mid range jumpers?

[2024-05-19 13:43] thewhitehope : Or I guess I should say does the range even matter if his OS is low
[2024-05-19 13:43] naph7777 : IS is shots from the post. OS is outside the paint, FT's and is a factor in 3P shooting. Range seems to be almost exclusively for 3 point shooting. Some guys can be effective from 3 with just high Rng, even with low OS.
[2024-05-19 13:44] thewhitehope : Ahhhh
[2024-05-19 13:44] thewhitehope : Okay well that's def helpful
[2024-05-19 13:45] thewhitehope : So really IS is for the post OS is for midrange with some impact on other shooting attributes and range is more indicative of his ability to hit 3's
[2024-05-19 13:46] naph7777 : Finishing is layups, dunks and non-post interior scoring. I'm not really sure how and when IS and Fin overlap.
[2024-05-19 13:46] thewhitehope : Awesome I was wondering about that too. So if you got a guy with a high driving score but his finishing sucks his driving is really gonna be helpful for dishing
[2024-05-19 13:46] naph7777 : For example if you shoot a shot in the post, it misses and you get the offensive rebound..... is the putback IS or Fin?
[2024-05-19 13:47] naph7777 : Yeah, drive and dish is still a thing. I figure a high finish, low drive guy, might still be okay cutting off the ball. A low finish, high drive can get anywhere on the floor, but will blow the layup more often than you'd like.

Players appear to have a certain preference for each shot/play-type and then you try and modify it further using the positioning instruction.

[2024-06-17 13:01] naph7777 : High interest is High interest.  It may take a D1 team less contacts to also get to High interest, but it is a significant investment of contacts to get to High against any team, and once there you have a significant chance of losing to another team on High.
[2024-06-17 13:02] naph7777 : Yes, I've been the minnow that gets to High first and then gets beat out on recruits that I've dumped lots of contacts into, but I've also successfully gotten guys who I could never have gotten if I'd waited to spend contacts until they were seniors.
[2024-06-17 13:03] maverick1993 : I’m also very new haha, but some sound advice I received is also to look at recruits in your region first. Identifying solid players in your region and being the first to high will be really helpful.
[2024-06-17 13:04] maverick1993 : Because out of state or out of region players cost more contacts then in state or in region.
[2024-06-17 13:04] naph7777 : I still largely avoid out of region recruiting that isn't in Canada or INTL.
[2024-06-17 13:09] naph7777 : I know its a while ago, but if you look at my post about my ECU rebuild https://discord.com/channels/410154227860504588/567195205430804511/1235021476550148160 you can see the sorts of guys I managed to get in LL6 and LL5. I don't think I could have gotten a number of those guys, and certainly not without spending a lot more contacts.
[2024-06-17 13:28] thewhitehope : So the division difference matters but it doesn't matter so much that i shouldn't battle a higher division team for a player if ive put points in him and gotten him to high?
[2024-06-17 13:34] naph7777 : Its always opportunity cost.  Is doing X the best use of my contacts?  It also depends on how many contacts it took you to get that player to High interest. If you got there in 25 contacts, then you know you're building  interest relatively quickly. If it took you 50 or 60 contacts, then its still going to take you another 24 or whatever just to get to Very High.
[2024-06-17 13:38] naph7777 : In general, a higher division team will take less contacts to reach the same level of interest. Which means that if you get into a battle where both teams are adding their 2 contacts in each day until the player signs.... then again, in general, the higher division team will slowly build an interest lead and the longer it goes on, the greater their chance of signing the player. (This is an assumption and seems to match people's experience. All I know officially is that Steve has revealed that spending more contacts after Very High does make a difference.)
[2024-06-17 13:46] naph7777 : In general I try and avoid fights, but you don't want to be the guy with a reputation for being easily pushed around either.  So mix things up a bit.   If a guy was a bit more expensive to get to High, maybe you don't spend any more contacts and you just hope what you've spent is enough. If a guy was cheaper to get to High and you don't have better options, maybe you go to Very High and hope he commits early. Maybe you even go all in until he commits.  Sometimes its worth hoarding your contacts for a while so it looks like you are dropping them all into your current board, when actually you are hedging your bets so you have a pile of contacts to use to pivot to someone else if your first target doesn't pan out.
[2024-06-17 13:47] naph7777 : /ramble   dunno how useful that all is. But I hope you get the general gyst of things. IMO it is not really as simple as "When this happens you should always do X". That's part of why I still enjoy the game.

[2024-06-17 17:58] freewynd : Does recruiting continue through conf playoffs or if you didn't land a senior yet they are going juco?
[2024-06-17 18:00] naph7777 : - Recruiting Calendar The recruiting calendar is broken into 53 updates (one after each game day). At the beginning of the season you'll receive a large sum of recruiting points followed by 2 points for every daily update thereafter. You can use recruiting point to contact a prospect and encourage them to come to your school. Starting with the 5th recruiting update, high school seniors will begin committing to schools. Junior college sophomores and international players will start committing later. On update #53, all uncommitted players will either commit to a school (given a valid scholarship offer), proceed to junior college (and continue to be recruited), become a walk-on at some program or leave basketball altogether.   I believe players can commit all the way up the 53rd recruiting update.

[2024-06-30 12:45] fatherborf : so i looked at the dev data for athletes i developed for at least 3 seasons over RITs last 6 seasons
[2024-06-30 12:45] fatherborf : and i may include other teams athletes now since all the data is public, but wanted to start with as few variables as possible and RIT has had the same coach and strat for 6 seasons
[2024-06-30 12:46] fatherborf : and basically i think whoever said that player dev is mostly dictated by their HS dev was spot on
[2024-06-30 12:47] fatherborf : sample size is still small, (<20 players) but it seems like HS dev and potential set the baseline development for an athlete, and stuff like coaching dev skills, playtime, etc, all simply act as small modifiers for that
[2024-06-30 13:00] fatherborf : even including my ridiculous outlier lincoln morris who developed 99 points in college vs his 49 in HS, on a development per season basis with ten 12pots, five 11pots, and two 10pots they averaged 11.43 dev per season vs 13.42 in college - without morris it shrinks to 11.35vs12.78  On a dev-per-game-played basis the gap is even smaller, 0.395 vs 0.430, only about 8%. again, remove morris, and it becomes 0.392 vs 0.405, only ~3% difference.  im going to keep collecting data and look for if there are noticable trends, but my intuition right now says that you can basically think of HS Dev as "100% expected development" and then other factors such as play time and coaching development raise or lower that, with some RNG thrown in for the occasional freaks that develop 90-100+ points like morris, which i think is a cool thing to include as a reflection of the real life randos who pick up a sport late or only become good at it very late.   for context on how wild Morris was, the 17 players avged ~115% of their HS development while in college. Morris redshirted, and totaled 202% of his total HS development while averaging 19.8 per season in college vs 12.3 in HS, i so far have had no one else come close to this gap for bates or RIT

[2024-07-03 02:56] lassoball : What marriage advice do you have, HW? Tying the knot this weekend 🪢
[2024-07-03 03:25] naph7777 : Congrats!  Talk.  Make time for each other. (This may not be a problem at the moment, but life happens)  Have a designated time/process for bringing up the stuff that's never the "right time" to bring up. Use it early and often. I suggest sitting or laying beside each other and talking about the problem in front of you both rather than across from each other and having the problem between you.  Accept that a number of things about your partner won't change. You can ask nicely if they'd consider/try changing them, but most won't change and/or there will be regression. If the benefits didn't outweigh these little frustrations you wouldn't be getting married. Love that they put up with your flaws. It makes it easier to put up with theirs.  Don't keep score. Either on the positives or the negatives. Do nice things "just because".  The hardest parts of a marriage are the early years after the honeymoon period. There's a reason "seven year itch" and the like is a trope. Both commit to not giving up when it gets hard. Then you can get to the really good parts of marriage, and not have to re-do the hard years again with someone else, and with more baggage.   Marriage is awesome. I'm so glad I'm not single.
[2024-07-03 03:39] lassoball : Thank you for this, <@453580403366821899> .  Just read this with my fiancée — so much good stuff here
[2024-07-03 03:49] naph7777 : The active listening thing: 1) Person A gets to talk about 1 thing until they are talked out 2) Person B has to state back what they heard. 3) Person A gets the clarify things they didn't say, misunderstandings or things important to them that were missed in person B's summary etc 4) repeated 2 + 3 until Person A feels heard 5) Return to 1 until everything both people want to talk about has been talked about.  Seems super-lame.   But its amazing how often what you think you said isn't what the other person hears. Being able to do this cuts out a lot of mind-reading, wondering why the other person is pissed off, or why you're having the same discussion/argument again and again. At the very least you both feel heard, even if you don't agree.

[2024-07-10 21:59] rivalmejr : Why is zone useful
[2024-07-10 22:02] thewhitehope : 3 basic defenses in this game. More in real life but here there's basically 3. Man to man. Zone. And pressure. Man to man means once the other team brings the ball across the half court line your defenders will all have a man (default would be the other guy at their position) and they would just play defense on that guy wherever he goes. Pressure is basically the same thing but instead of waiting till half court they pick them up all the way at the other end of the court when they inbounds the ball.
[2024-07-10 22:03] thewhitehope : Zone means each of your five players is assigned a zone on the floor they have to defend. When the offensive player comes in their zone they start defending them, when the offensive player leaves his zone he stops defending him. As a simplistic explanation
[2024-07-10 22:04] thewhitehope : Man to man is easier to pull off with better players and zone allows a team with less defensive ability to still be effective defensively.
[2024-07-10 22:06] rivalmejr : Ah okay!
[2024-07-10 22:06] rivalmejr : So right now zone because my team sucks
[2024-07-10 22:07] rivalmejr : But since I have been hyper focusing on defense I imagine in the future I'll be a better suited for man to man

[2024-07-16 17:14] infinite_tea : You don’t set it — it’s just the number of times that your team ended up in transition (this didn’t have time to set a defense). It’s usually off of turnovers, and fast pace teams force you into transition more than slow pace teams.

[2024-07-16 17:38] infinite_tea : Probably. Or his turnovers occurred at more opportune times (for fast break opportunities).
[2024-07-16 17:40] infinite_tea : Or, he had the same amount of fast break opportunities but fewer possessions overall (so the percentage of fast break to overall possession just makes it look like more than you).
[2024-07-16 17:46] cdilks : .36 x 3 is bigger than .53 x 2. And if they're taking that many threes, that's the number you want to push lower.

[2024-07-17 13:48] thewhitehope : How do the substitutions work insofar as if I put my starting point as backup for sg... he'll never play sg right?
[2024-07-17 13:50] naph7777 : The key line in the rules is: "Note: positions will be filled in the following order: PG, C, PF, SF and SG. So if you have one player as the primary backup for both guard spots - if both starters are on the bench, then the backup player will fill in at PG and the game engine will move to the next position on the depth chart to grab a SG."
[2024-07-17 13:51] thewhitehope : So because PG is the primary position, he'll always run as PG
[2024-07-17 13:52] naph7777 : Then you combine that with the section about Subsitution Modes. And you can work out, at least near the start of the game before people hit foul/minutes restrictions who will sub-in/sub-out and what position they will play.
[2024-07-17 13:52] thewhitehope : Okay cool thank you much
[2024-07-17 13:52] naph7777 : Its a bit annoying and I wish you were allowed to tweak the fill order. But it is, what it is.

[2024-07-18 01:35] jerbeetwo : “Also note, the checkbox in the Game Management section needs to be checked at the end of the season for the player to actually be red shirted.” This sentence in the Help Manual has me confused.  Here is my situation.  I took over my teams after the flip and after game 4 of non conference.  I redshirted some freshmen but I am confused by this sentence.  Is this the redshirt season for those freshmen?  Or will the box being checked at the end of THIS season make NEXT season be their redshirt season?
[2024-07-18 01:39] thewhitehope : It'll be this season. So as long as u don't play them more than 5 games and that box is checked at the end of the season then this year will count as their redshirt
[2024-07-18 01:54] naph7777 : The magic time for the checkbox is during the season flip. Checking it early will make it less likely that the CPU randomly subs in a redshirt and has them playing games that might make the ineligible to redshirt. (Set them to 0 minutes after they have played 5 games just to be safe).  Its like that, because people can change their mind mid-season. Maybe you were going to redshirt a guy, but there's some key games late that will decide promotion/demotion for example. In that situation maybe you decide that you will play a guy that was going to redshirt even though they have missed half a season. Its rare, but it does happen.  So essentially, you have made the decision to redshirt certain players, but the actual redshirt decision doesn't happen until the rollover at the end of this season. That's when the redshirt will be noted on their player profile and they will change from FR -> RS FR, instead of going FR -> SO (for example, you can also redshirt a SO or a JR)
[2024-07-18 02:06] cdilks : Also, Steve made a special note of it, and usually does a forum post about it, because every year someone forgets to check the box on someone they were hoping to redshirt.
[2024-07-18 02:58] stromstar : This usually happens during postseason exhibition games. If you don't make the tournament, you get placed in an Invitational group, and since they don't count as real games, it's a way to give redshirting players extra play time.
[2024-07-18 03:12] jerbeetwo : Thank you all for your help.
[2024-07-18 14:17] infinite_tea : Steve has changed the code on this — so even RS players will play as long as you (1) put them in the lineup and (2) give them minutes in Game Management.
[2024-07-18 14:18] infinite_tea : That said, I would recommend putting players to 0 minutes AND checking the RS box to ensure they don’t play 5 games. I’ve had cases in the past where I only checked the RS box, and they would sneak into a game when injuries would deplete my roster.
[2024-07-18 14:18] infinite_tea : I also always set my walk-ons to 10 mins per game, just to make sure they play before my RS players.

[2024-08-19 12:51] naph7777 : <@348063426628681729> welcome back! You've already played 17 seasons so I'm going to assume you have some idea.  Good time to rejoin as we are close to a season flip. 1) Consider changing your head coach before you spend your recruiting contacts. 2) Consider changing one or more assistant coaches before you spend your recruiting contacts. 3) Spend the next week having a look at the classes that teams in your conference signed. Particularly those who promoted. Look at other conferences at the same level. Try and work out what skills/attributes are prioritised and get a sense of what is attainable, and just as importantly what isn't at your level. 4) Don't go nuts and fill too many scholarships in one go. If you decide you just have to, then get some JuCo's or plan on redshirting some freshmen and not others to spread them out a bit.
[2024-08-19 12:52] thinscallops : Back in the game after a good bit away and wouldnt mind an overview of recruiting strategies, game tactics ect. I don't need to know any trade secrets only an update. Thanks...
[2024-08-19 12:52] thinscallops : Much appreciated!
[2024-08-19 12:53] naph7777 : Generally, my advice is spend your time working out what target(s) you want.... then when you decide to go in on a player, go hard. Especially down in the lower leagues you really want to jump straight to High (at least Medium) on your top target(s). Which normally means recruiting in-region and in-state.
[2024-08-19 12:54] naph7777 : If you aim too high and are only showing Medium interest... a bigger fish can jump to High with all the new contacts going around at the season flip. Then you're stuck in a hard place.
[2024-08-19 12:55] naph7777 : So either go early... get to High and prepare to fend off all-comers.... or cast a wider net and be more patient... sit on your contacts and let the big fish feed... then scoop the best of the rest once everyone else has spent their contacts.
[2024-08-19 12:57] thinscallops : With only two scholarships out I'll probably play the long game and try to establish a 4-4-4-4 recruiting strategy.
[2024-08-19 12:57] naph7777 : If you're trying to fill a bunch of scholarships... then the 2nd strategy should work better. Your competitive advantage with that many open scholarships is that a) recruits will correctly think they will get playing time, and b) you can give guys with lower SI (think graduating HS in the 70's-80's in SI) with decent (10+) potential and good evaluation comments more minutes. ie you can give them the minutes to develop into their evaluation comments... whilst better teams wouldn't be able to play them and be competitive..... So you want guys that have developed well in HS, but are still too low in current skill to get much attention.
[2024-08-19 12:58] naph7777 : Generally people redshirt all of their 3-star and below recruits. The extra year of development is hard to beat and there's only a small penalty for doing so.
[2024-08-19 12:58] naph7777 : 4-4-4-4 with no redshirts can certainly work. I generally aim to alternate 3-2-3-2-> etc and redshirt most guys.
[2024-08-19 13:05] naph7777 : If nobody better crops up, you could do worse than promoting assistant coach (AC) Matthew O'Reilly.

[2024-08-21 20:57] flushednevada : This is hard to answer, because there are so many variables. The long answer is that what matters more than the value at the end of their HS Sr year is their growth in that category since their HS Fr year. Comments are also a great way to gauge potential growth. I’d much rather have a recruit who finishes HS with 7 IS but projects to grow to 14 than a recruit who finishes with 10 IS but projects to never improve. You can see all this on the Development Graph on the prospect page (it’s in the drop down tab above Contact and Offer Scholarship).

[2024-08-29 07:14] naph7777 : Well you currently have SR: 0 JR: 2 SO: 0 FR: 6  So you've got some balance problems no matter what you do. I'd probably redshirt 3 freshmen. Not redshirt the other 3.  That would turn your 0-2-0-6 into 2-0-3-3 next year without signing any recruits this year. If you plan on redshirting most 3* and below players (like most managers) Then you could sign 2 guys this year and be on a  2-0-3-3-2 schedule. sign 3 the year after 0-3-3-2-3  keep alternative 2's and 3's from there and you have a nice sustainable pattern to take you upwards.    Some people prefer a less balanced plan so that they have more "up" years with 7 or more upperclassmen. The plan then being to promote when your team is older and just aim to hang on and not demote when you are younger. Up to you on what you want to aim for there.

[2024-09-02 19:38] .julioso : How do I stop my team from turning the ball over so much
[2024-09-02 19:38] .julioso : Slower pace on offense?
[2024-09-02 22:49] thewhitehope : That and in game management you can also raise your players to + with the thinking that if they're shooting it more they're not passing it as much resulting in a turnover
[2024-09-02 23:45] naph7777 : Pace will depend on the type of turnovers you are getting.  If you have lots of shot clock violations and passes leading to steals, then increasing green light on players and upping the pace makes sense.  If you’re throwing the ball away in transition and have lots of fumbling the ball to the other team then slowing the pace may help.  In general upping the green light settings helps the most, but often comes at a reduction in FG efficiency.

[2024-09-29 22:28] naph7777 : One exists for coaching comments. It only has the order of the player evaluation comments.   The ratings in HW are a bit “fuzzier” than BB (or at least so I have been told). So you can have a “very good post player” finish with higher IS than a capped out “dominating post scorer”, even though the latter is the “better” comment.  That’s why I didn’t put actual ranges for player comments.
[2024-09-30 01:15] naph7777 : Easiest way to get a feel for ballpark figures is to scroll through the top pros http://onlinecollegebasketball.org/top_pros  most of those players will have reached their peaks in all attributes.
[2024-09-30 02:07] mrmagic07 : 👍🏾
[2024-10-01 00:35] fatherborf : yeah comments are really good indicators but dont seem to work at all as necessarily accurate "limits" except for negative comments - for example i have a PG with "above average post moves" who is a RS SR, and maybe i get lucky and it pops a bunch now, but he only has 9 IS - for Bates my PG does not have a "long range shooter" comment, but has 18 range. and his only defensive comment is "Will never be a good interior defender." - and thats true, he only has 2 ID... but he has 18 PD. So comments like "Can be a decent rebounder" dont *guarantee* they will end up with precisely like 14-16 rebounding.
[2024-10-01 00:43] fatherborf : to simplify it as a broad concept to apply: if you are choosing between two similar recruits and one has a negative comment in a skill you value a lot, and the other has no comment at all, no comment is usually better. For someone with "Does not have much of a shooting touch" it is, as far as i know, impossible for them to have like 16 OS. I dont even think Ive had anyone who had a negative comment and were starting college at 5 or less in the skill, ever hit double digits in said skill, but ive not played nearly as long as a lot of these guys so there may be really notable exceptions. Some of my best players so far have kinda consistently been dudes who simply had like only 2 or 3 positive comments and zero bad ones and developed into players just as talented as any of my "good/excellent all around player" comment recruits
